scope: phase_C_ingress_delivery; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Watch delivery authorization/policy check occurs outside the delivery lock and is never revalidated through the transport scope
findings.issue: deliver_watch builds the AuthorizationRequest from the notification's data_class captured outside any lock, then only _guard_watch is re-run at transport time. _guard_watch checks lifecycle/quiet hours/quota but never _source_current or a re-run of registry._decision for the delivery grant, so a revocation occurring after the pre-commit reservation commit but before/while the sender runs does not fail closed: the effect still proceeds and is recorded as sent.
findings.fix: Inside the transport scope lock, re-run the final delivery decision for every class and re-check _source_current (or hold a FOR SHARE grant lock that spans the sender), raising CapabilityDenied/leaving the attempt unknown before any transport call if any grant is no longer allowed.

findings.title: Media file_id minimum-length bound is not enforced (only upper bound)
findings.issue: For document/photo intake the code checks len(selected['file_id'])>512 but never checks non-emptiness, unlike the voice path which requires 0 < len(file_ref). An empty file_id passes intake validation and is persisted and queued.
findings.fix: Apply the same 0 < len(selected['file_id']) <= 512 bound (and reject empty/non-str) before constructing media_input.

findings.title: watch.py archive collector uses wall-clock datetime.now despite the scheduler fixture clock, breaking deterministic scheduling tests
findings.issue: wire_archive_watch.collect computes now=datetime.now(timezone.utc) while the scheduler/collection code path is driven by scheduler.clock; with a fixture clock the produced due_at values can be far in the past or future relative to the guarded active window, making behavior non-deterministic and not testable per project rules.
findings.fix: Derive 'now' from the scheduler's clock (or pass the current guard timestamp into the collector) so collected notifications are deterministic and aligned with subscription expiry checks.

not_verified: prm/storage/jobs.py, policy.py, watch_jobs.py, actions.py, deletion.py and bot/* integration are not in the supplied packet; queue fencing, grant reservation semantics, and PAI-09 delivery attempt gating could not be independently verified.
Runtime behavior against real PostgreSQL was not executed; conclusions are from static source review of the supplied modules and tests.
Whether _decision/authorize_and_reserve internally re-checks grants under the transport transaction (which would downgrade finding 1) is outside the supplied sources.
findings.summary: Static review of the supplied C_ingress_delivery modules and tests found no P0: intake dedup/owner scoping, one-use versioned confirmations, coalesced scheduler advancement, unknown-outcome no-retry, and chunked aggregate fencing are implemented with clear fail-closed paths and are meaningfully tested. One P1 remains: watch delivery never revalidates policy inside the final transport scope (unlike answer delivery, which runs _source_current), so a revocation racing the send can still produce an actual effect after authorization was withdrawn. Two smaller P2s cover an unbounded-empty media file_id and non-deterministic wall-clock use in the archive watch collector. Fix the watch delivery revalidation before ship.
